## Further Reading

Borthick, A. F., Schneider, G. P., & O'Brien, A. D. (2024). Developing business process and query skills for solving business problems. *Issues in Accounting Education*, *39*(3), 99–108. <https://doi.org/10.2308/issues-2023-053> In this case, learners follow a business process diagram for the sales and returns of a car dealer and its manufacturer, and then query a database to find out why the two parties' dashboards disagree. It practices the operations of this chapter, joining tables, aggregating data, and verifying that a query is correct, and it can be worked in any SQL system.

Cooper, R., & Kaplan, R. S. (1992). Activity-based systems: Measuring the costs of resource usage. *Accounting Horizons*, *6*(3), 1–13. <https://doi.org/10.2308/ah-9604083361> The authors set out the conceptual basis of activity-based cost systems, which measure the cost of the resources that activities use, and they treat the cost of capacity that is supplied but not used separately, as a volume variance. The distinction helps in reading a plant that records more hours than its output requires.

Datar, S. M., & Rajan, M. V. (2021). *Horngren's cost accounting: A managerial emphasis* (17th ed.). Pearson. <https://www.pearson.com/en-us/pearsonplus/p/9780136713845> A standard cost accounting text. Its chapters on flexible budgets and on direct-cost and overhead variances explain how standard costs are set and how actual inputs are compared with the inputs allowed for the output achieved, the framework behind the manufacturing variance that this Part investigates.

Farkas, M., Kersting, L., & Stephens, W. (2016). Modern Watch Company: An instructional resource for presenting and learning actual, normal, and standard costing systems, and variable and fixed overhead variance analysis. *Journal of Accounting Education*, *35*, 56–68. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jaccedu.2016.02.001> This instructional resource takes students through actual, normal, and standard costing on one set of data, with particular attention to overhead variances and the fixed overhead production volume variance. It is a useful companion to the controller's question of whether a variance comes from volume or from cost.

Li, J., & Lee, L. (2021). Teaching data joins: A conceptual approach using SQL, Alteryx, and Tableau. *AIS Educator Journal*, *16*(1), 60–104. <https://doi.org/10.3194/1935-8156-16.1.60> A three-part assignment that teaches inner, left, right, and full outer joins in several tools, and that asks students to select, use, and validate joins. It is a good next step for anyone who wants to see how the join types of this chapter appear outside SQL.
